chapter: State of the country and the anthem
title: Music as a way to bridge differences, Obama and Beyonce with the Marine Band
summary: Jang describes performing the national anthem in different versions, being class president, and views on Obama's use of the arts.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Well, so my role, and I’ll go back, I was elected ninth grade president. Because I think people, they like me, either my personality, I mean I had relationships with the jocks, who were generally more conservative, I had relationships with more of the alternative artists, intellectual hippy types. And if I perform the “Star Spangled Banner” National Anthem, depending on the context, I can perform it in the tradition of John Phillip Sousa on the piano, or I can first perform it in the traditional way and then go into another version and then come back to it. So I can take music and bring people — it helps resolve the differences. So it’s kind of like hey, we all share the same food, we can all go out to different restaurants, but we all don’t have to like certain foods. And so that’s the same thing. Different versions of the National Anthem. And I also have friends who, you know, they react to — how can I describe it — I want to try to be respectful — say of the Tea Party republicans. To me there is — you know you don’t want to be emotionally reactive to that either. Because that also doesn’t really — I guess it’s kind of crisis management or anger management. And actually in some ways I thought Barack Obama was trying to unite the country. And I’ll give you an example. I like the idea of having Beyonce collaborate with the Marine Band. I liked the idea. However, Barack Obama is not an artist or involved in cultural production. So if you want to have that collaboration, and you want to quote unquote arts to succeed, you have to have it inside. Or you have to have both of them be prerecorded, and can kind of accept that. And I think, as I said before, the American Bandstand legacy, we forget about that. And we also forget that, hey, what is the big deal about that, because I mean MTV — the emphasis is on the visual aspect. I mean Michael Jackson or anybody else cannot dance and sing at the same time. That’s too – when we hear singers, whether it’s opera — their instrument is the voice. And it’s very difficult to do that.
